title: Exploring Causal Effect of Social Bias on Faithfulness Hallucinations in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Manipulating gender attributes in multiple-choice question-answering templates to create Pro-stereotype, Anti-stereotype, and Non-stereotype contexts, and measuring the causal effect on faithfulness/unfairness hallucinations using Individual Causal Effect (ICE).
Substituting religious identities and beliefs in contextual QA scenarios to evaluate the causal relationship between religious stereotypes and the hallucination rates of Large Language Models.
Altering socioeconomic status indicators (e.g., wealthy vs. poor, low-income) in text templates to perform pairwise comparisons of model hallucinations under different bias intervention states.
Modifying age-related attributes and character descriptions in prompt templates to assess whether age-based stereotypes cause the model to generate unfairness hallucinations.
Changing social attributes related to physical and cognitive disabilities in reading comprehension scenarios to quantify the causal impact of disability biases on model output faithfulness.
